aviso.idioma_del_corpus: Legal text is shown in the official language of its source, untranslated. The interface is translated, the law is not: a translation of ours would no longer be the law.
aviso.latido.apagado: The heartbeat is off, which is how it ships. Nothing leaves this machine towards us.
aviso.latido.arregla_callado: Test the channel with plazum latido probar and check this machine's internet access.
aviso.latido.arregla_fallo: Test the channel with plazum latido probar and look at what the destination answers.
aviso.latido.arregla_nunca: Test the channel with plazum latido probar.
aviso.latido.callado: No heartbeat has arrived for %d hour.|No heartbeat has arrived for %d hours.
aviso.latido.fallo: The last heartbeat attempt did not arrive.
aviso.latido.late: The last heartbeat went out fine %d hour ago.|The last heartbeat went out fine %d hours ago.
aviso.latido.no_es_tu_planificador: This is the channel from this machine towards us. Its silence does not mean your deadlines stopped being watched: the verdict above is computed with your clock and without going out to the network.
aviso.latido.nunca: The heartbeat is on and none has gone out yet.
aviso.planificador.arregla_callado: Run a cycle with plazum latido ciclo and check the timer that launches it. We warn once it goes over %d hours without running.
aviso.planificador.arregla_futuro: Set the machine clock right and wait for the next cycle.
aviso.planificador.arregla_nunca: Schedule plazum latido ciclo every hour, in cron or in a systemd timer. There is an example in docs/latido.md.
aviso.planificador.arregla_sin_instante: Tell us about it, this should not happen.
aviso.planificador.callado: Your scheduler has not run for %d hour. While it stays stopped, deadlines pass with nobody watching them.|Your scheduler has not run for %d hours. While it stays stopped, deadlines pass with nobody watching them.
aviso.planificador.futuro: The last scheduler mark is in the future, so we cannot tell you whether it is alive. It is usually the machine clock, not plazum.
aviso.planificador.late: The scheduler is alive. Its last run finished %d hour ago.|The scheduler is alive. Its last run finished %d hours ago.
aviso.planificador.nunca: The scheduler has not run a single cycle yet. If you have just installed plazum that is normal, if it has been installed for days it is not.
aviso.planificador.sin_instante: We do not know which instant to judge from, so we cannot tell you whether the scheduler is alive. That is our fault, not yours.

uar.aviso.sin_autor: There is no record of who is operating, and a fact without an author is not a fact. Sign in again before deciding.
uar.cierre.que_es: Closing means signing that everything has been reviewed. If anything is unreviewed or a line is unexcused, plazum will not let you close and says exactly what is missing.
uar.duplicadas: %d row of the file repeated an access already listed and is not reviewed twice.|%d rows of the file repeated an access already listed and are not reviewed twice.
uar.error.render: The page could not be rendered.
uar.excusar.deja_rastro: An excuse is recorded with your name and your reason, and it appears in the report. It is not a way to make it go away, it is a way to answer for it.
uar.excusar.hasta: To line (leave empty for a single one)
uar.identidad.reproducible: With that file in hand, anyone can repeat the reading and check that this, and nothing else, is what was reviewed.
uar.ilegibles.bloquean: They block closing. Nobody knows what was there, so completeness cannot be certified. Fix it in the file, or excuse it in writing below.
uar.ilegibles.titulo: %d line of the file could not be read as an access|%d lines of the file could not be read as accesses
uar.no_consta: This does NOT say these accesses are improper: it says that in this campaign there is no record of anyone having reviewed them.
uar.no_revisado.cuantos: %d access is still unreviewed.|%d accesses are still unreviewed.
uar.sin_campana.paso1: First upload the file, which is what seals the campaign:
uar.sin_campana.paso2: Then start the server telling it which files those are:
uar.sin_campana.por_que_el_fichero: Both are needed because plazum does not store your list of people: the rows are read from the file every time, and the record only holds what was decided.
uar.sin_campana.que_es: An access review campaign is a list of accounts and permissions that someone looks at one by one and approves or revokes. Plazum does not invent it: it comes from the file your IdP exports.
uar.sin_campana.titulo: There is no campaign here yet
uar.sin_revisor: %d access has no reviewer assigned. This is said now and not at closing time: a warning that arrives when nothing can be done about it is not a warning.|%d accesses have no reviewer assigned. This is said now and not at closing time: a warning that arrives when nothing can be done about it is not a warning.
uar.sin_sesion.por_que: This is the only page in plazum whose content is people's names and their permissions. Serving it to someone who has not signed in would turn it into a staff directory published by accident, so it is not rendered.
uar.sin_sesion.titulo: Sign in to see this page
uar.sin_token: This session cannot change anything: the session token is missing. Sign in again and the buttons come back.
uar.tabla.pie: What is reviewed is the access, not the person: someone can stay in the company and still have one permission too many.
